item.title: ICS Calendar Invite Phishing Hides Base64 Lures and QR Credential Harvesting
item.content:encoded:
The Phishing Kit That Rode In on a Calendar Invite — Should Read

A phishing email hid its entire credential-harvesting lure inside an .ics calendar invite, using embedded images, a personalized link, and a QR code to bypass body-focused email scanning. The key lesson is that defenses must inspect and render calendar attachments, including OCR and QR decoding, instead of treating them as harmless scheduling data.

  • A freight and logistics company received a phishing email whose body was nearly empty, with the malicious content hidden inside an .ics calendar invite attachment.
  • The .ics file contained a multi-page internal compliance lure rendered as embedded base64 images, along with a personalized credential-harvest link and a QR code encoding the same URL.
  • The phishing URL used the recipient’s own corporate email address in the path, allowing the landing page to appear personalized to that mailbox.
  • The message reached the inbox even though a Barracuda gateway scored it benign and Microsoft assigned it a trusted spam confidence level of -1.
  • IRONSCALES Themis flagged the message at 90% phishing confidence after rendering and OCRing the embedded images, decoding the QR code, and correlating sender and relay mismatches.
